newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SCALA ALREADY REAPING RICH HARVEST WITH DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCALA ALREADY REAPING RICH HARVEST WITH DORTMUND.

text.p: As the son of a farming family, Nevio Scala knows it takes time and patience to produce a good harvest.

But the new Borussia Dortmund coach is already reaping the benefits of the seeds he sowed in pre-season training and is hoping his work bears more fruit on Saturday, when the European Cup winners take on UEFA Cup holders Schalke in the league.
Scala, who took over from Ottmar Hitzfeld in the close season, is an enthusiastic proponent of attractive soccer, peppered with short passes and aggressive pressing of opponents.
Those elements were used to great effect in Dortmund's 3-0 demolition of Cologne in midweek.
And, worryingly for local rivals Schalke and Dortmund's other opponents over the coming weeks, the coach reckons his crop of stars will get better with every game.
"I've planned my training programme so that we only reach our peak in a couple of weeks from now," he said.

"We're on our way to putting Nevio Scala's attacking philosophy into practice," confirmed defender Juergen Kohler, who was last week voted Germany's player of the year. "We'll have reached our top form in four weeks."
Schalke coach Huub Stevens was in Dortmund's Westfalen Stadium on Wednesday night to check out the home side ahead of Saturday's Ruhr Valley derby and could not fail to be impressed.
"They're top fit and amazingly quick. Simply superb," admitted the Dutchman, whose side had lost 2-1 to Duisburg the previous evening.
But Scala, who still helps out on the family farm back home in Italy when time allows, faces a struggle to persuade his players that he knows best how to cultivate success.
The ex-Parma coach favours playing with just one striker, instead of the twin-pronged approach usually used by Hitzfeld.

"It's difficult to say which strategy is better," Dortmund's attacking midfielder Lars Ricken said. "We've already played some very good games with only one real striker but we've also played some very bad ones."
Scala stuck to two strikers -- Stephane Chapuisat and Heiko Herrlich -- in Dortmund's opening game of the season, a 1-1 draw with Hertha Berlin last weekend.

But with Chapuisat on international duty in midweek, the Italian took the opportunity to switch to his favoured system against Cologne, playing Herrlich on his own with Andy Moeller providing the link between midfield and attack.
The result was impressive. Dortmund looked good, won comprehensively and Herrlich was among the scorers.
Now Dortmund fans are asking whether Scala will risk his flourishing crop by reintroducing Chapuisat against Schalke.
